subject: Pen test: infrastructure coverage & boundary rules
messages:
From: Alice Cheng <alice.cheng@atlanticbank.com>
To: dylan.brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: pt@acme-sec.com
Date: Wed, 17 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pen test request — what falls inside scope?

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for the quick intake call earlier. Acme Security is lined up to run Atlantic Bank's penetration test against Redwood-managed components on June 6–8. Before we publish the engagement letter, security asked for a clear, one-page definition of what "in scope" means from Redwood's side. Specifically: whether Hosted API, Dedicated instances, Private (VPC) deployments, and on-prem installations are included — and if so, what surfaces (control plane, data plane, customer-managed network egress, model artifacts) are tested.

Could you confirm:
- Which hosting variants Redwood will make available to the testers (agent access, jump hosts, test accounts)?
- Are customer-managed VPCs considered in-scope only with customer opt-in?
- Do dedicated GPU pools for Dedicated customers belong to a tenant-scoped test or are they treated as isolated/shared infra?

We need this to finalize the scoping matrix and produce the artifact for Atlantic's compliance team. Attaching Acme's standard scoping checklist for reference.

Appreciate your guidance — Alice

Attachment: acme_scoping_checklist.pdf (application/pdf)

From: dylan.brooks@redwood.ai
To: Alice Cheng <alice.cheng@atlanticbank.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, pt@acme-sec.com
Date: Wed, 17 May 2028 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pen test request — what falls inside scope?

Alice — thanks, quick response below and looping Rishi and Laura for technical and legal confirmation.

High level proposed boundary:
- Hosted (Redwood API): IN-SCOPE. Testers may exercise API endpoints, request/response paths, and the hosted control plane tenant metadata. We will provide a dedicated test tenant and API keys; no access to other customers.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): PARTIAL. Per-tenant GPU pools are in-scope only for customers who sign the test authorization (we treat these as tenant-scoped systems). Shared scheduler/orchestration components are in-scope as platform services.
- Private / VPC-hosted (customer-managed): OUT-OF-SCOPE by default. If Atlantic Bank provisions a Private deployment and explicitly requests Redwood-assisted testing, we will run an agreed subset limited to the Redwood-managed control plane services. We will not perform testing inside customer-managed private networks without separate contract addenda.
- On-prem installations: OUT-OF-SCOPE unless a formal on-prem engagement is contracted and a Redwood engineer is granted host-level access.

Next steps: Rishi to provide a short mapping table of hostnames, services, and recommended test account credentials. Laura to confirm wording for the authorization letter and SLA addendum. Once we have the scope matrix we will attach the infra diagram and sign the engagement.

Serving as the point of contact on scheduling — Dylan

--
Dylan Brooks
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
dylan.brooks@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0132

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: dylan.brooks@redwood.ai, Alice Cheng <alice.cheng@atlanticbank.com>, pt@acme-sec.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 17 May 2028 13:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pen test request — what falls inside scope?

Adding the technical boundaries and minimal artifact list below — please treat as the canonical mapping for test rules. I kept it short so Acme can integrate it into their checklist.

Scope matrix (summary):
- Hosted API (hosted.redwood.ai tenant test account): IN-SCOPE
  - Services: API gateway, inference runtime containers (per-tenant), request logging pipeline (metadata only), monitoring endpoints.
  - Not in-scope: multi-tenant control plane database host that stores cross-tenant billing aggregates (read-only simulated data provided).
  - Test access: API keys + a sandbox corpus; no live customer data.

- Dedicated (reserved GPU pools):
  - If customer has a dedicated reservation and explicitly signs the test authorization: in-scope for that tenant's GPU nodes, associated model artifacts stored in tenant buckets, and the dedicated network namespace.
  - If not authorized: only platform-level endpoints (scheduler, placement) are in-scope; tenant nodes stay out.

- Private / VPC (customer-managed):
  - Redwood-managed control plane endpoints that accept telemetry/heartbeats: IN-SCOPE (we can provide a test endpoint).
  - Any customer-hosted compute, bastions, or private subnets: OUT-OF-SCOPE unless Atlantic provides explicit access and secures an on-site statement of work.

- On-prem installations: OUT-OF-SCOPE by default. We require a separate on-site engagement, runbooks, and explicit physical access authorizations to include these systems.

Required artifacts for engagement:
1) asset inventory (hostnames, CIDR ranges, service tags) — see attached scope_matrix.csv
2) test account/API keys with stated TTL (we recommend 72 hours)
3) maintenance windows and escalation contacts
4) signed testing authorization and SOW (legal)

Known constraints and mitigations:
- We will not provide production DB dumps or live customer PII.
- For Dedicated customers, we can enable a readonly snapshot of scheduler logs for Acme if needed.
- If Atlantic wants Private deployment testing, procurement must request the Private-testing addendum (we'll provide pricing for onsite/remote options).

Attachment: scope_matrix.csv (text/csv)

Rishi Malhotra
Director, Platform Security | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai

From: Acme Security <pt@acme-sec.com>

Cc: Alice Cheng <alice.cheng@atlanticbank.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Pen test request — what falls inside scope?

Thanks everyone, that is very helpful and actionable. Two quick requests before we finalize the engagement letter and test window:

1) Please upload the redwood_infra_diagram.pdf and the scope_matrix.csv to the shared Drive link you control (we referenced https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/pt-scope/atlantic-2028). We prefer Drive-hosted artifacts with a short expiry.

2) We will need a signed authorization PDF and the optional PT SLA addendum (if Atlantic needs extended hours). Laura — can you confirm the wording for the authorization and attach pt-sla-addendum.pdf?

Operational notes:
- We will use the tenant test keys for all authenticated checks. No social-engineering of Redwood staff will be performed unless explicitly authorized.
- For Dedicated nodes that are in-scope, our default is to limit intrusive destructive testing to a defined time box; please indicate whether Atlantic accepts that constraint.

If you can upload the artifacts and confirm authorization language by EOD Friday (2028-05-19), we will ship the engagement letter and schedule test engineers.

Regards,
Marcus (Acme Engagement Lead)
Acme Security
